statement_as_printed: the Kd ... amounted to 6 uM as determined by ITC, with a 1:1 stoichiometry

topic: binding: full-length Keap1 with N-terminal Nrf2 domain
statement_as_printed: Even in the presence of 100 uM RA839 an interaction between Keap1 and the N-terminal domain of Nrf2 was detectable.

exposure: 1, 10, 100 uM RA839 in 1% DMSO, 5 h at room temperature

note: Fig. 5 shows the anti-FLAG signal progressively weaker at 10 and 100 uM in the two lanes pairs (inferred_from_figure); the text says 10 uM did not affect binding. The authors speculate that cell concentrations affect mainly the DLG (weaker) interaction rather than full dissociation (Discussion; declared, not tested). Whether the compound dissociates full-length Keap1 from Nrf2 in cells is not shown.

statement_as_printed: EC500 of 49 +/- 8 uM (concentration for 5-fold induction)

topic: array result: overlap with Keap1 silencing

note: Check from Fig. 6 (my arithmetic): 59/105 = 56.2 %; (59+9+3)/105 = 67.6 %. Of 105 RA839 probe sets, 34 are RA839-only (32 %). The authors call the overlap "only moderate" and name siRNA off-target and 48 h secondary effects as possible reasons (Discussion).

statement_as_printed: Canonical pathways for RA839: glutathione biosynthesis (Gclc, Gclm, Gss), Nrf2-mediated oxidative stress response (Gsta3, Gclc, Aox1, Gclm, Txnrd1, Mafg), eNOS signalling (Prkar2b, Prkaa2, Figf), L-serine degradation (Srr)

topic: NO and Nos2 in the Nrf2 knock-out arm (with compound)

The inference of Nrf2 dependence of Nos2 repression rests on concordance of three activators, and the paper itself says "Further studies will have to show" whether the same mechanism (p300 recruitment, as in microglia) operates in BMDM.
